votemeta.desc: A measure to place a binding referendum on the March 2024 ballot asking voters to convert the city's flat real-estate transfer tax into a graduated 'mansion tax,' raising rates on property sales above $1 million to fund homelessness services. The Council voted 32-17 to put it on the ballot; voters narrowly rejected the referendum in March 2024.

A non-binding resolution calling for a permanent ceasefire in the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza. Mayor Brandon Johnson cast a rare tie-breaking vote in favor in January 2024, making Chicago the largest U.S. city at the time to pass such a resolution.

A series of Council actions over the city's ShotSpotter (SoundThinking) gunshot-detection contract, which Mayor Johnson moved to cancel as a campaign promise. The Council repeatedly pushed back, voting 34-14 in May 2024 and again in September 2024 to limit the mayor's ability to end the contract. ('Affirmative' here reflects support for ending/canceling the contract.)

Anti-displacement housing protections for South Shore and the area around the future Obama Presidential Center, the product of a decade-long community campaign. The Jackson Park Housing Pilot — drawing on the South Shore Housing Preservation Ordinance — passed in September 2025, offering affordable set-asides, a right to return, and home-repair funds.

votemeta.full: Paid Leave & Paid Sick Leave Ordinance
votemeta.desc: An ordinance requiring most Chicago employers to give workers 10 paid days off a year — five sick days and five for any reason — among the most expansive municipal paid-leave laws in the nation. The Council passed it 36-12 in November 2023; implementation was later delayed to July 2024.

An ordinance championed by Ald. Brian Hopkins (2nd) in response to downtown 'teen takeovers,' letting the police superintendent declare a curfew anywhere in the city with 30 minutes' notice. The Council passed it 27-22 in June 2025, but Mayor Johnson vetoed it — his first veto — and the Council failed to override in July 2025.

A signature Johnson housing initiative creating a city-backed nonprofit (the Residential Investment Corporation) to run a $135 million revolving loan fund for permanently affordable, mixed-income, sustainable housing. The Council approved it 30-18 in May 2025, making Chicago the first major U.S. city to adopt the model.

A 2026 effort to halt the 'One Fair Wage' phase-out of the tipped subminimum wage that the Council adopted in 2023 (which was raising tipped pay toward the full minimum wage by 2028). The Council voted 30-18 in March 2026 to freeze the phase-out; Mayor Johnson vetoed the freeze, and in April 2026 the Council fell short of overriding it, so the phase-out continued. ('Affirmative' here reflects support for repealing/freezing the phase-out.)
